source_name: AHK Ukraine (German-Ukrainian Chamber) — 'Закупівлі та тендери' donor tender guide
why_relevant: Curated Ukrainian-language directory explaining that UA contracting authorities receiving EBRD/World Bank/EIB loans procure under donor rules rather than national law, and pointing to each donor's portal. Excellent snowball map of donor procurement entry points for a local audience.

source_name: Ukraine-Britain Business Council — outline of IFI-financed procurement opportunities in Ukraine
why_relevant: Maps the actual landscape of IFI-financed procurement channels in Ukraine, naming Prozorro plus RELINK, REPOWER, DREAM and PREPARE alongside EBRD and World Bank portals — a compact actor/portal map for this cell and the origin of several leads to verify.

source_name: DevelopmentAid — donor tender/award aggregator (Ukraine)
why_relevant: Commercial aggregator that mirrors WB/EBRD/UN/EU notices with structured metadata and organisation profiles (confirmed Ukraine WB procurement-specialist tender and an IFC Ukraine org profile). Useful as a cross-check and for retrospective coverage of expired notices.

source_name: NISS (National Institute for Strategic Studies) — monthly 'Допомога міжнародних фінансових інститутів Україні'
why_relevant: Monthly Ukrainian-language analytical series tracking IFI assistance flows to Ukraine (Jan/Feb 2026 editions found), naming instruments, lenders and amounts. Gives the funding context that explains which procurement pipelines are about to open, in official Ukrainian terminology.

source_name: MDB harmonisation of procurement in Ukraine (World Bank press release, Oct 2023)
why_relevant: The founding document of the CEB/EBRD/EIB/World Bank harmonised approach for UA public-sector investment procurement. Defines the rule regime and thresholds that determine whether a donor-financed UA contract appears on a lender portal or in Prozorro — the routing logic this whole cell depends on.

source_name: TED — Tenders Electronic Daily (Supplement to the Official Journal of the EU)
why_relevant: Canonical EU-level publication channel for contract notices and contract award notices above EU thresholds. Captures EU-institution and EU-funded contracts naming Ukraine, contracts of EU delegations/missions in Ukraine, and contracts where Ukrainian entities appear as tenderer/awardee — awards that frequently never appear in any Ukrainian national channel.

source_name: TED Developer Docs — Search API
why_relevant: Documents the machine-readable route into TED: expert query language, field names, notice XML (eForms) bulk download. This is the difference between an ad-hoc lookup and a durable monitored feed for Ukraine-linked banking/payments contracts.

source_name: SIMAP / European Public Procurement legal bases (on TED)
why_relevant: Explains the publication obligation, thresholds and notice taxonomy that determine WHAT is guaranteed to appear in TED — essential for judging coverage completeness and for interpreting Ukraine's accession-driven alignment with EU directives.

source_name: EU Funding & Tenders Portal (SEDIA)
why_relevant: Single entry point for procurement run directly by Commission DGs, agencies and executive bodies, including DG NEAR technical assistance touching Ukraine's financial sector. Complements TED (many calls appear here with richer documentation than the OJ notice).

source_name: DG NEAR — Grants and Tenders (Enlargement and Eastern Neighbourhood)
why_relevant: DG NEAR is the contracting authority for most EU external assistance to Ukraine, including financial-sector and public finance management technical assistance. This page routes to the specific calls, frameworks and award publications.

source_name: Ukraine Facility (European Commission topic hub)
why_relevant: The 2024–2027 EUR 50bn instrument is the funding envelope behind a large share of Ukraine-linked contracting, including digital/payments infrastructure and public finance modernisation. Gives the pipeline and reform milestones that precede procurement, so it is a leading indicator for future notices.

source_name: EEAS — Tenders (European External Action Service)
why_relevant: Central listing of EEAS/EU delegation procurement, including below-threshold negotiated procedures that never reach TED. Relevant to cash handling, security-of-value, IT and banking-services contracts of EU bodies operating in Ukraine.

source_name: EUAM Ukraine — Procurement / Tenders
why_relevant: EU Advisory Mission Ukraine runs its own CSDP-mission procurement in-country (IT, equipment, services) outside TED thresholds. A distinct EU-level channel where Ukrainian vendors appear as awardees.

source_name: EU4DigitalUA — Procurement page
why_relevant: Directly in-cell: an EU-funded project (implemented by the e-Governance Academy, Estonia) procuring digital identity, Diia portal software, electronic ID/signature and IT equipment in Ukraine. Digital ID and e-signature are adjacent infrastructure to payments/KYC, and the notices name the real implementing contractors.

source_name: EU NEIGHBOURS east — Opportunities (calls for tender)
why_relevant: EU regional communication platform that aggregates calls for tender across Eastern Partnership EU-funded projects, including EU4DigitalUA component-leader tenders. Useful as a snowball hub to discover project names and implementers that then lead to primary notices.

source_name: EBRD Client e-Procurement Portal (ECEPP)
why_relevant: Cross-border IFI channel: procurement, prequalification, shortlisting and contract award notices for EBRD-financed and EBRD-administered-grant projects in Ukraine, including financial-sector reform, procurement-practice reform and banking-related consultancy. Ukrainian banks appear as clients/borrowers.

source_name: European Investment Bank — Ukraine financing packages / procurement
why_relevant: EIB Group operations with the Commission under the Ukraine Investment Framework create downstream procurement by Ukrainian public entities and on-lending through Ukrainian banks. Press releases name counterparties and sums ahead of any notice.

source_name: Mission of Ukraine to the EU — EU public procurement market guide for Ukrainian exporters
why_relevant: Ukrainian-language official explainer of how Ukrainian firms (incl. fintech/IT/financial services) access EU tenders via TED and the WTO GPA (Ukraine acceded 18 May 2016). Gives the local terminology and the legal basis for Ukrainian entities appearing as awardees on foreign portals — the core of this cell.

source_name: Prozorro Infobox — Ukraine Facility procurement rules explainer
why_relevant: Explains, in Ukrainian, how EU Ukraine Facility money is procured (national law plus Framework Agreement requirements) — i.e. exactly which EU-funded contracts land in Prozorro rather than TED. Critical for de-duplicating and for knowing where NOT to look.

source_name: Prozorro — International donor procurement news section
why_relevant: Dedicated Ukrainian-side stream on donor-funded and foreign-country procurement, i.e. the bridge between the national system and EU/IFI channels. Announces where and how donor tenders (incl. EU) are published, which surfaces cross-border opportunities involving Ukrainian banks/PSPs.

source_name: TED third-party mirrors and search wrappers (HAD.de EU invitations to tender, TenderWolf, Tendersontime, Jorpex)
why_relevant: Mirrors and re-indexers of TED that sometimes expose better free-text search, alerting or historical retention than the official UI. Useful as a cross-check that a Ukraine-linked notice was not missed, and for spotting CPV/keyword combinations that work.

source_name: TED / EU procurement open-data dataset listings (data.europa.eu and derivatives)
why_relevant: Bulk historical TED notice datasets allow retrospective analysis — e.g. every award since 2016 whose text mentions Ukraine or a Ukrainian bank — which the live search UI cannot do efficiently. Supports trend and competitor-share analysis over time.

source_name: Spending — Єдиний веб-портал використання публічних коштів (transaction search)
why_relevant: Near-real-time State Treasury payment transactions searchable by payer (розпорядник) and payee (контрагент), with payment purpose text. This is the ground-truth layer showing which vendor actually got paid for ATM/POS/processing equipment and services, in what amount and when — including recurring maintenance payments that never re-appear as new tenders.

source_name: E-data Spending API (api.spending.gov.ua) — transactions endpoint
why_relevant: Machine-readable access to treasury transactions with startdate/enddate parameters; the practical backbone for any longitudinal tracking of who is paid for banking hardware and services.
